callerTrace: EngineImageSmoke.__init__ generates a new secrets.token_urlsafe(32) password; no CLI/environment/installation-password argument is accepted for it.
EngineImageSmoke.qualify admits native Linux/amd64 host and Docker daemon plus a real writable /dev/shm tmpfs mount before creating the secret fixture.
The sole non-unit call passes self.pg_env[POSTGRES_PASSWORD] to the helper in its new TemporaryDirectory. All other references are synthetic unit controls.
Engine commands replace the direct password with a deliberately wrong fixture value and bind the exact secret inode readonly at /run/engine-db-password to qualify the real _FILE loader.

artifactAndCleanup: Secret path is outside output_dir; engine evidence artifact upload selects production-engine output only.

findings.intrinsicBoundary: The real _FILE loader must receive the actual password bytes. Encrypting/substituting that mounted payload would stop testing this file-secret contract. This does not imply plaintext filesystem storage is required for every possible credential API.

callerTrace: Fixture constructs its own TemporaryDirectory, local source members, synthetic configuration, random plaintext marker and two newly generated restic password files.
All put callsites use literals, newly generated secrets.token_hex values, or file bytes read from that same owned fake snapshot; negative DNS/URI inputs remain synthetic observer fixtures.

RealResticDescriptorTests and RealResticTests use only those temporary source/key/repository/restore paths. Environment input selects a restic executable/opt-in flag, not a key, source-data file or remote repository.

Recovery Command replaces inherited environment with an allowlist; restic --repo and --password-file are explicit generated local fixture paths. No ambient RESTIC_PASSWORD or provider credential is inherited.
fileAuthority: Absolute descriptor walk with O_NOFOLLOW for each ancestor
At least one owned0700 private ancestor required
Leaf must be owned single-link regular file, no-follow/nonblocking open
Existing inode is restricted to0600 before truncation or payload write; key writes retain0600
artifactAndCleanup: The real workflow keeps fixtures/results under private and uploads only reports, with sanitized diagnostics.
Fixture.close removes the entire temporary tree and asserts absence; workflow tracks descendant processes, requires fixture emptiness and cleanup, and retains no plaintext source/key artifact.
The encryption test deliberately scans actual repository bytes for the random source marker, verifies restore, wrong-key failure and tamper rejection.
This is local synthetic cryptographic/descriptor qualification; it proves neither off-host custody nor restored installed application acceptance.
findings.intrinsicBoundary: A plaintext source marker is necessary to test that real file backup encrypts that marker and restores identical bytes. Real restic reads the generated password via the adapter’s explicitly qualified password-file contract. Using generated fixtures rather than installation secrets is the relevant scope boundary.

residualLimits: Generated test credentials are still plaintext while in use. Host root and the same OS user can inspect process/filesystem/container state.
tmpfs is not a no-swap guarantee; engine report correctly leaves swapPolicyAttested false. Recovery test temporary files may use disk.

Unlink/TemporaryDirectory cleanup is not secure erasure. SIGKILL/host failure can bypass Python finally blocks; ephemeral runner teardown is an additional lifecycle boundary, not installed secret-custody proof.
Helpers accept general bytes/strings and cannot prove random provenance by type alone; the generated-only conclusion is based on all inspected current callers and their pinned sources.
No new runtime, live Docker, crypto, cleanup or CodeQL run was executed by this read-only review.
